recommended_high_slope_source.source: Ducas, Stevens, van Woerden, 'Advanced Lattice Sieving on GPUs, with Tensor Cores', EUROCRYPT 2021 (ePrint 2021/141; CWI final version), Fig. 7(b), triple_gpu fit

lattice_practical_slope.reason: It is the highest-dimension author fit (sieving dims 121-140) on the GPU record-setting hardware class, and the measured FLOP counts of the actual records (Table 1, MSD 127-150) give the same slope (0.365/dim), so it is the best-supported upper estimate of the practical per-dimension growth. The BGJ-family slope (bgj3: 0.314, dims 70-100) and ZDY's 0.2925 gate model sit between it and the 0.292 asymptotic low end.
lattice_practical_slope.usage_note: Apply both slopes per SIEVING dimension: compare the record's max sieving dimension (171) with the target's sieving dimension beta' = beta - d4f (Kyber R3 Table 4: 375/586/829), not with beta (413/637/894). Derived example (MSD 171 -> beta'): delta = 204/415/658, low 0.292*delta = 59.6/121.2/192.1, high 0.367*delta = 74.9/152.3/241.5 log2 units. These are per-sieve-call ratios. A full BKZ/primal attack adds a polynomial number of calls (the Kyber spec's gate count uses (d - beta)*C ~ 2^9.3 extra for Kyber-512).

decodingchallenge_complexity_model.statement: Documentation page, 'Indication of complexity': 'This number is computed by multiplying the length n by the workfactor of Dumer's algorithm for the parameters of the challenge. The workfactor is computed with the Cawof software. This value is only given for informational purposes.'
decodingchallenge_complexity_model.unstated: No memory-access cost is stated. CaWoF (Canto Torres-Sendrier workfactor tool) counts operations in the RAM model, i.e. effectively constant-cost memory, but the site does not say so explicitly. The unit is a rounded integer exponent (tooltips like '2^63').

frontier_tooltips.caveat: Every QC tooltip equals w exactly (QC_10 -> 2^10 ... QC_160 -> 2^160). This is consistent with ~(1-R)^-w = 2^w, but the exact equality across all 76 instances suggests a closed-form 2^w rather than a CaWoF Dumer computation. Treat as indicative.

same_model_crypto_size_analog.value: Goppa track n=3471 (k~0.8n, w=58) tooltip 2^142; n=3545 tooltip 2^144. Nearest same-model instances to mceliece348864 (n=3488, k=2720, w=64), but with different k and w.

target_model.statement: Esser-Bellini Syndrome Decoding Estimator (SDE; PKC 2022, ePrint 2021/1243) reports bit complexity including polynomial factors. memory_access=0 means constant-cost memory (optionally capped), 1 = logarithmic, 2 = square-root, 3 = cube-root memory access cost.
target_model.source: SDE source estimate_code_based_nist_schemes.py (labels 'M < mem' / 'Logarithmic' / 'Square-root' / 'Cubic-root memory access' for memory_access 0/1/2/3)

code_model.consistency: Not directly consistent. decodingchallenge = n * Dumer workfactor (CaWoF), constant-cost memory implied, Dumer only. The SDE tables give the best of Prange/Stern/Dumer/BJMM/May-Ozerov/Both-May, under either constant cost (memory_access=0) or sqrt cost (memory_access=2). No source found tabulates SDE estimates for the frontier instances (Goppa n=1409, QC n=4098, SD n=570). A like-for-like comparison therefore requires either (a) running SDE/CryptographicEstimators on the frontier instances (not done: no downloaded code executed), or (b) a simple shared model. For (b), plain Prange iteration counts log2[min(C(n,w), 2^(n-k)) / C(n-k,w)] (Prange 1962) are fully specified. Derived here: Goppa-1409 (k=1127, w=26) 61.7; SD-570 (k=285, w=70) 60.0; QC-4098 (k=2049, w=64) 64.7; mceliece348864 142.8; mceliece460896 184.9; mceliece6688128 262.4; mceliece6960119 263.4; mceliece8192128 300.1; hqc-128 key problem (n=35338, k=17669, w=132) 132.4 before the ~log2(k)/2 = 7.0 DOOM/QC discount. These Prange counts are within ~1.3 bits of the decodingchallenge tooltips at frontier sizes (63/64/60). At crypto sizes, advanced ISD gains ~20 bits over Prange under the sqrt model (SDE, mceliece348864: Prange 178.3 vs May-Ozerov 158.6), so a Prange-based gap overstates the advanced-ISD gap by up to ~20 bits for McEliece. Same-model decodingchallenge gap 1409 -> n=3471 Goppa-track analog: 142 - 63 = 79 bits.

ecdlp_check.statement: The rho method breaks ECDLP using, on average, approximately 0.886 sqrt(l) additions; 0.886 = sqrt(pi/4) (includes the negation-map speedup). Table: NIST P-256 2^127.8, secp256k1 2^127.8, Curve25519 2^125.8.
ecdlp_check.formula: sqrt(pi*l/4) group additions (batched affine short-Weierstrass additions)
ecdlp_check.source: Bernstein and Lange, SafeCurves, 'The rho method' page

rsa_check.statement: Table 2 'Comparable security strengths of symmetric block cipher and asymmetric-key algorithms': security strength 112 <-> IFC (RSA) k = 2048 (also FFC L=2048/N=224, ECC f=224-255, 3TDEA). 128 <-> k=3072; 192 <-> k=7680; 256 <-> k=15360.
rsa_check.source: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 (May 2020), Section 5.6.1.1, Table 2 (pp. 54-55)

HQC-128/192/256 under the square-root memory model: Esser-Bellini PKC 2022 Table 4 not retrievable (ePrint and iacr.org archive return 403). Only constant-memory SDE values (via Wu-Zhuang 2022) are recorded. Wu-Zhuang do not state the memory model or whether the QC/DOOM discount is applied.

Esser-May-Zweydinger EUROCRYPT 2022 ('McEliece needs a Break') experimentally calibrated extrapolations for McEliece/HQC not retrievable (403). Per the abstract, they confirm BIKE/HQC levels and find McEliece 192/256-bit sets overestimated by ~20/~10 bits.

No source tabulates SDE/CryptographicEstimators estimates for the decodingchallenge frontier instances (Goppa 1409, QC 4098, SD 570). Computing them requires running the estimator (Python+C from GitHub), which was not done. The derived Prange-iteration comparison in code_model.consistency is the substitute.
decodingchallenge's CaWoF unit and memory model are not stated on the site. QC-track tooltips equal w exactly for every instance, which suggests a closed form rather than a CaWoF computation.

Zhao and Ding, 'Towards Large-Scale Lattice Attack: New Lattice Records by Disk-Based Sieving' (Springer 2026, the likely bgj3-gpu record paper) is paywalled; any timing fit it reports was not read. The public BGJ-Sieve-GPU README contains no fit.
Original source of the SVP-186 (4x A100, 50.3 d) record cited in ZDY Table 5 was not identified; its FLOP count (2^71.4) is ZDY's estimate.
Lattice-estimator: the README shows only Kyber-512 and does not name the default reduction cost model; Kyber-768/1024 estimator outputs not recorded.

rsa_frontier_check.model: F(b) = (64/9)^(1/3) * (b ln 2)^(1/3) * ln(b ln 2)^(2/3) / ln 2; leading GNFS expression, o(1) omitted
rsa_frontier_check.interpretation: Derived model ratio, not observed cost or calibrated wall-time/dollar prediction. Only common size-independent multiplicative factors cancel; omitted size-dependent terms do not. NIST 112 is not an endpoint in this calculation.
rsa_frontier_check.consistency_claim: Primary write-up estimates RSA-2048 roughly one billion times harder than RSA-1024, and 91.2 billion times RSA-260; these use similar GNFS scaling, not independent measurements.
